evidence: Offensive content has become pervasive in social media and a reason of concern for government organizations, online communities, and social media platforms. One of the most common strategies to tackle the problem is to train systems capable of recognizing offensive content, which then can be deleted or set aside for human moderation. In the last few years, there have been several studies published on the application of computational methods to deal with this problem. Most prior work focuses on a different aspect of offensive language such as abusive language BIBREF0 , BIBREF1 , (cyber-)aggression BIBREF2 , (cyber-)bullying BIBREF3 , BIBREF4 , toxic comments INLINEFORM0 , hate speech BIBREF5 , BIBREF6 , BIBREF7 , BIBREF8 , BIBREF9 , BIBREF10 , and offensive language BIBREF11 . Prior work has focused on these aspects of offensive language in Twitter BIBREF3 , BIBREF7 , BIBREF8 , BIBREF11 , Wikipedia comments, and Facebook posts BIBREF2 .

title: Predicting the Type and Target of Offensive Posts in Social Media
answer_short: Offensive language is language that is directed at an individual, a group, or other entities, and can be categorized as insults, threats, or profanity.
answer_rationale: The definition of offensive language is derived from the hierarchical annotation model described in the documents, which categorizes offensive language by type (insults, threats, profanity) and target (individual, group, other). This model is used in the OLID dataset to annotate offensive language in social media, as detailed in Text 1 and Text 5.
